housing: Hillingdon is London's second-largest borough, with 1930s Metro-land semis in Ruislip, Eastcote and Ickenham, larger houses in Northwood, and denser terraces and estates in Hayes and West Drayton. Private renting rose by almost 8 percentage points between 2011 and 2021, one of the biggest rises in London, to about a quarter of households. Heathrow and Brunel University drive demand for shared homes and HMOs, and the council has brought in borough-wide additional HMO licensing and Article 4 planning controls on new HMOs. New-build flats are going up around Hayes and Uxbridge.
checkinTips: Shared homes let to airport workers and Brunel students: photograph each bedroom's lock and smoke alarm, the shared kitchen, and the fire doors and their closers.
Extended Metro-land semis in Ruislip and Eastcote: photograph loft rooms, rear extensions and their rooflights, and any ceiling stains below flat roofs.
Homes near Heathrow in Harlington, Hayes and West Drayton: photograph windows, seals and any secondary glazing or acoustic vents fitted against aircraft noise.
Gardens and driveways on family houses: photograph lawns, fences, sheds and the drive surface at check-in.
New-build flats in Hayes and Uxbridge: record fob, parking and post-box key counts and photograph balconies and integrated appliances.
tenantHelp: Private tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions to Hillingdon Council's private sector housing team, which takes complaints from tenants and can inspect and take enforcement action.
